subproblem.title: The Euclidean coefficient norm is a Euclidean norm pulled back by a continuous linear map
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers and Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n, the space of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P. Let |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (∑_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where (e_j) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun). Then there is a continuous linear map A : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) with |α| = ‖A α‖ (Euclidean norm) for every α ∈ Λ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ A : Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α = ‖A α‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the coefficient map 𝒜). Its continuity is proved directly here, without appealing to finite dimension.
Notation: e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j is the j-th standard basis vector of ℝ^P. For I : Fin n → Fin P, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) ∈ (ℝ^P)^n.
1. (Coordinate functionals.) Fix I : Fin n → Fin P. Define ev_I : Λ → ℝ by ev_I(α) := α(e_I).
   - ev_I is linear, because the vector-space operations of Λ are pointwise.
   - ev_I is continuous, because |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖ (operator norm of α; each ‖e_j‖ = 1).
   In Mathlib, ev_I is ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ e_I. Define the continuous linear functional c_I := ev_I if I is strictly increasing, and c_I := 0 otherwise.
2. (The map A.) Let A₀ : Λ → ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ), A₀(α) := (c_I(α))_I. A map into a finite product is continuous linear when each coordinate is, so A₀ is continuous linear (ContinuousLinearMap.pi). Let A := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n → Fin P) ℝ).symm ∘ A₀, the composition with the continuous linear identification of the function space with EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P). Then A is continuous linear, and (A α)_I = c_I(α) for every I.
3. (The norm identity.) Let α ∈ Λ. By the formula for the Euclidean norm (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), ‖A α‖ = (∑_I |c_I(α)|²)^{1/2}, summed over all I : Fin n → Fin P. For each I:
   - if I is strictly increasing, then |c_I(α)|² = α(e_I)²;
   - otherwise |c_I(α)|² = 0² = 0.
   So |c_I(α)|² = (if StrictMono I then α(e_I)² else 0). Comparing the sums term by term (Finset.sum_congr) gives ‖A α‖ = (∑_I (if StrictMono I then α(e_I)² else 0))^{1/2}. This is literally the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm α. Hence |α| = ‖A α‖ for all α ∈ Λ, and A is the required map.
proof_key_steps: Each coefficient α ↦ α(e_I) is a continuous linear functional (|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖). It is replaced by 0 when I is not strictly increasing.
Bundle the coefficients into a continuous linear map A into EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) via ContinuousLinearMap.pi and EuclideanSpace.equiv.
EuclideanSpace.norm_eq and the termwise identity |if c then a else 0|² = if c then a² else 0 give ‖A α‖ = covectorEuclideanNorm α.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree without additional hypotheses. Each coefficient evaluation is continuous linear independently of finite-dimensionality; the finite product followed by EuclideanSpace.equiv constructs A. EuclideanSpace.norm_eq gives precisely the defining coefficient sum. The inferred target norm is L². The supplied proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: The space of n-covectors on ℝ^P is finite-dimensional
subproblem.statement: For all natural numbers P and n, the real vector space Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P is finite-dimensional.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), FiniteDimensional ℝ (Covector (Euclid P) n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (Tietze) of the parent proof uses the fact 'Λ is a finite-dimensional real vector space' without proof. Mathlib has no such instance for continuous alternating maps, so the fact is proved here.
1. Let e = (e_j)_{j ∈ Fin P} be the standard basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ, regarded as a basis of the module Euclid P).
2. Define Φ : Λ → ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ) by Φ(α)(v) := α(e_{v(0)}, …, e_{v(n−1)}). Addition and scalar multiplication in Λ are pointwise, so Φ(α + α') = Φ(α) + Φ(α') and Φ(cα) = cΦ(α). Hence Φ is ℝ-linear.
3. Φ is injective. Suppose Φ(α) = Φ(α').
   - The underlying alternating maps of α and α' (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap) are n-linear. They take the same value on every n-tuple of basis vectors (e_{v(0)}, …, e_{v(n−1)}).
   - An n-linear map is determined by these values. Write each argument as w_k = ∑_j w_k^j e_j and expand by multilinearity: α(w_0, …, w_{n−1}) = ∑_{σ : Fin n → Fin P} (∏_k w_k^{σ(k)}) α(e_{σ(0)}, …, e_{σ(n−1)}), and likewise for α'.
   - So the two alternating maps are equal (Mathlib Module.Basis.ext_alternating, which only needs agreement on injective σ).
   - A continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). Hence α = α'.
4. The codomain (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ is finite-dimensional: its index set is finite, and its dimension is Pⁿ. A vector space with an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective). Therefore Λ is finite-dimensional.
proof_key_steps: Evaluation on all n-tuples of standard basis vectors is a linear map Φ from Λ into the finite-dimensional space (Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ.
Φ is injective: multilinear maps that agree on basis tuples are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating), and a continuous alternating map is determined by its underlying alternating map.
An injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space forces finite dimension (FiniteDimensional.of_injective).

audit.reason: The exact type expresses the stated finite-dimensionality for arbitrary P and n. Evaluation on all basis tuples is linear and injective by alternating-map extensionality, and its codomain is finite-dimensional. FiniteDimensional.of_injective completes the proof, including zero-dimensional and empty-index cases. No child or parent result is assumed.

subproblem.title: Compactly supported continuous unit-norm extension of a covector field from a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n and |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm. Let K ⊆ V ⊆ ℝ^P with K compact and V open. Let β : ℝ^P → Λ be continuous on K with |β(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ K. Then there is a continuous g : ℝ^P → Λ with compact support such that tsupport g ⊆ V, |g(x)| ≤ 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P, and g(x) = β(x) for every x ∈ K.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (K V : Set (Euclid P)) (β : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n), IsCompact K → IsOpen V → K ⊆ V → ContinuousOn β K → (∀ x ∈ K, covectorEuclideanNorm (β x) ≤ 1) → ∃ g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n, Continuous g ∧ HasCompactSupport g ∧ tsupport g ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (g x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, g x = β x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0 and 2–5 of the parent proof (Tietze extension, radial retraction onto the unit ball of |·|, cut-off). The only change: the cut-off radius r is chosen with cthickening(r, K) ⊆ V, which is all that is needed here.
0. (Empty K.) If K = ∅, take g := 0. It is continuous; tsupport 0 = ∅ is compact and contained in V; |0| = 0 ≤ 1 (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero); and the condition on K is vacuous. From now on assume K ≠ ∅.
1. (Norm facts.) By the sibling coeff_norm_rep, fix a continuous linear map A : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) with |α| = ‖A α‖ for all α. Then:
   (N1) α ↦ |α| is continuous, as the composition of A with the norm;
   (N2) |cα| = ‖A(cα)‖ = ‖c·A α‖ = |c|·|α| for every c ∈ ℝ.
2. (Tietze.)
   - K is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P, hence closed. ℝ^P is a metric space, hence normal.
   - The restriction β|_K : K → Λ is continuous (ContinuousOn.restrict).
   - By the sibling covector_finite_dimensional, Λ is a finite-dimensional real Hausdorff topological vector space. So it has the Tietze extension property (Mathlib instance RCLike.instTietzeExtensionTVS from Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.Tietze).
   - Hence there is a continuous B : ℝ^P → Λ whose restriction to K is β|_K (ContinuousMap.exists_restrict_eq). That is, B(x) = β(x) for all x ∈ K.
3. (Retraction.) For α ∈ Λ put m(α) := max(1, |α|) ≥ 1 > 0 and ρ(α) := m(α)⁻¹·α.
   - By (N1), m is continuous and never 0, so m⁻¹ is continuous and ρ is continuous.
   - By (N2), |ρ(α)| = m(α)⁻¹|α| ≤ 1, because |α| ≤ m(α).
   - If |α| ≤ 1, then m(α) = 1 and ρ(α) = α.
4. (Cut-off.) K is compact and the open set V contains K. So there is r > 0 with cthickening(r, K) = {x : infDist(x, K) ≤ r} ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Define χ(x) := max(0, 1 − infDist(x, K)/r).
   - x ↦ infDist(x, K) is continuous (1-Lipschitz), so χ is continuous.
   - infDist ≥ 0, so 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1.
   - For x ∈ K, infDist(x, K) = 0, so χ(x) = 1.
   - If infDist(x, K) ≥ r, then 1 − infDist(x, K)/r ≤ 0 and χ(x) = 0. So every x with χ(x) ≠ 0 satisfies infDist(x, K) < r, i.e. x ∈ thickening(r, K). This uses K ≠ ∅ (mem_thickening_iff_infDist_lt). Hence support χ ⊆ thickening(r, K).
5. (The field g.) Put g(x) := χ(x)·ρ(B(x)). It is continuous, as the product of the continuous scalar function χ and the continuous map ρ ∘ B.
   (a) Support: g(x) ≠ 0 forces χ(x) ≠ 0, so support g ⊆ thickening(r, K). Then tsupport g = closure(support g) ⊆ closure(thickening(r, K)) ⊆ cthickening(r, K) (closure_thickening_subset_cthickening) ⊆ V.
   (b) Compact support: cthickening(r, K) is closed and bounded in ℝ^P, hence compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper). tsupport g is a closed subset of it, hence compact. So g has compact support.
   (c) Bound: for every x, |g(x)| = χ(x)·|ρ(B(x))| by (N2) and χ ≥ 0. Since χ ≤ 1 and |ρ| ≤ 1 (step 3), |g(x)| ≤ 1·1 = 1.
   (d) Agreement on K: let x ∈ K. Then χ(x) = 1 and B(x) = β(x) with |β(x)| ≤ 1. By step 3, ρ(β(x)) = β(x), so g(x) = 1·β(x) = β(x).
6. Hence g is continuous with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere, and g = β on K.
proof_key_steps: If K = ∅, take g = 0. Otherwise |·| = ‖A·‖ gives continuity and homogeneity of |·|.
Tietze: Λ is finite-dimensional, so β|_K extends to a continuous B : ℝ^P → Λ.
Retract radially: ρ(α) = max(1,|α|)⁻¹α is continuous, |ρ| ≤ 1, and ρ = id on {|α| ≤ 1}.
Cut off with χ = max(0, 1 − infDist(·,K)/r), where cthickening(r,K) ⊆ V. Then g = χ·(ρ∘B) is continuous, tsupport g ⊆ cthickening(r,K) ⊆ V is compact, |g| ≤ 1, and g = β on K.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and conclusions match. The proof handles empty K, applies Tietze using the finite-dimensionality sibling, obtains continuity and homogeneity from the coefficient sibling, and verifies the radial retraction and cutoff. The support closure lies in a compact thickening contained in V; the global unit bound and exact agreement on K follow. Both declared dependencies are necessary to the supplied route and correctly directed.

subproblem.title: Mollification of a compactly supported continuous unit covector field
subproblem.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, Λ := Covector (Euclid P) n with operator norm ‖·‖, and |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm. Let V ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Let g : ℝ^P → Λ be continuous with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ V and |g(x)| ≤ 1 for every x. Let ε > 0. Then there is an n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λ that is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω), with tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, and |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (ε : ℝ), IsOpen V → Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → tsupport g ⊆ V → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (g x) ≤ 1) → 0 < ε → ∃ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ V ∧ (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x) ≤ 1) ∧ ∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm (ω x - g x) ≤ ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (mollification), applied to an arbitrary compactly supported continuous field g with |g| ≤ 1 and tsupport g ⊆ V. Two changes from the parent: the support margin r is chosen from tsupport g, and the constant in (N5) is the operator norm of the coefficient map. Any finite constant works there.
1. (Norm facts.) By the sibling coeff_norm_rep, fix a continuous linear map A : Λ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P) with |α| = ‖A α‖ for all α ∈ Λ. Let C₀ := ‖A‖ ≥ 0 be its operator norm. Then
   (N5) |α| = ‖A α‖ ≤ C₀‖α‖ for all α.
2. (Support margin.) tsupport g is compact (g has compact support) and contained in the open set V. So there is r > 0 with cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).
3. (Uniform continuity.) A continuous function with compact support is uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). So there is s₀ > 0 such that ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(C₀ + 1) whenever dist(y, x) < s₀. Put s := min(s₀, r) > 0.
4. (Kernel.) Let φ be the smooth bump function ContDiffBump (0 : ℝ^P) with rIn = s/2 and rOut = s. Let ψ := φ.normed volume be its normalization for Lebesgue measure. Then:
   - ψ is C^∞, ψ ≥ 0 and ∫ ψ = 1;
   - support ψ = B(0, s), the open ball;
   - tsupport ψ is the closed ball, so ψ has compact support;
   - ψ is continuous and integrable.
   (ContDiffBump.contDiff_normed, nonneg_normed, integral_normed, support_normed_eq, hasCompactSupport_normed, continuous_normed, integrable_normed.)
5. (Definition.) Let ω := ψ ⋆ g, that is ω(x) = ∫ ψ(t)·g(x − t) dt. In Mathlib this is convolution ψ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, a Bochner integral in the complete space Λ. For each x, the integrand t ↦ ψ(t)·g(x − t) is continuous and vanishes outside the compact set tsupport ψ, hence integrable (HasCompactSupport.convolutionExists_left, ConvolutionExistsAt.integrable).
6. (Smoothness.) ψ is C^∞ with compact support, and g is continuous, hence locally integrable. So ω is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left, with smoothness order ⊤).
7. (Support.)
   - ψ and g both have compact support, so ω has compact support (HasCompactSupport.convolution).
   - support ω ⊆ support ψ + support g (support_convolution_subset).
   - If y = t + z with ‖t‖ < s and z ∈ support g ⊆ tsupport g, then dist(y, z) = ‖t‖ < s, so y ∈ thickening(s, tsupport g). Thus support ω ⊆ thickening(s, tsupport g).
   - Hence tsupport ω ⊆ closure(thickening(s, tsupport g)) ⊆ cthickening(s, tsupport g) ⊆ cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V, using s ≤ r and step 2.
   Together with step 6, ω is C^∞ with compact support (IsTestForm ω) and tsupport ω ⊆ V.
8. (Bound |ω| ≤ 1; this is (N4) of the parent.) Fix x. A is continuous linear and the integrand of step 5 is integrable, so A commutes with the integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm) and with scalar multiplication: A(ω(x)) = ∫ ψ(t)·A(g(x − t)) dt. Hence
   |ω(x)| = ‖A(ω(x))‖ ≤ ∫ ‖ψ(t)·A(g(x − t))‖ dt = ∫ ψ(t)·|g(x − t)| dt ≤ ∫ ψ(t) dt = 1.
   This uses norm_integral_le_integral_norm, ψ ≥ 0, |g| ≤ 1, monotonicity of the integral (integral_mono_of_nonneg; ψ is integrable) and ∫ ψ = 1.
9. (Approximation.) Fix x.
   - For every y ∈ B(x, s), dist(y, x) < s ≤ s₀, so ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ ≤ ε/(C₀ + 1) by step 3.
   - Since ∫ ψ = 1, ω(x) − g(x) = ∫ ψ(t)·(g(x − t) − g(x)) dt. Because ψ ≥ 0 and support ψ ⊆ B(0, s), only t with ‖t‖ < s contribute, i.e. those with x − t ∈ B(x, s). So ‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ ε/(C₀ + 1). This is ContDiffBump.dist_normed_convolution_le; g is a.e.-strongly measurable because it is continuous.
   - By (N5), |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ C₀‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ C₀·ε/(C₀ + 1) ≤ ε.
10. Steps 6–9 show that ω is C^∞ with compact support, tsupport ω ⊆ V, |ω| ≤ 1 everywhere, and |ω − g| ≤ ε everywhere.
proof_key_steps: Choose r > 0 with cthickening(r, tsupport g) ⊆ V. By uniform continuity, choose 0 < s ≤ r with ‖g(y) − g(x)‖ < ε/(‖A‖+1) whenever dist(y,x) < s.
Convolve g with a normalized smooth bump ψ of radius s. Then ω = ψ ⋆ g is C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ cthickening(s, tsupport g) ⊆ V.
A commutes with the integral, so |ω(x)| ≤ ∫ ψ(t)|g(x−t)| dt ≤ 1.
dist_normed_convolution_le gives ‖ω(x) − g(x)‖ ≤ ε/(‖A‖+1), hence |ω(x) − g(x)| ≤ ε.

audit.reason: The statement includes every required hypothesis and matches its Lean proposition. The proof establishes a support margin, positive smoothing radius, normalized nonnegative kernel, integrability, smoothness, and compact support inside V. Commuting A with the integral proves the unit bound; uniform continuity and C₀ = ‖A‖ give the global ε estimate. Covector completeness is independently available, so no finite-dimensionality dependency is missing. The proof uses only the declared coefficient sibling and library results, and combines with the extension child to prove the selected parent.
